title: Bengali Prepositions and Postpositions
summary: Use common Bengali postpositions for location, direction, time, comparison, means, cause, and relationships.

phrases.en: The book is inside the bag.
He is inside the room.
The children are playing outside.
The book is on the table.
The bird is sitting on top of the tree.
The cat is under the table.
The boat is beneath the bridge.
He sat beside me.
The school is near my house.
The market is far from here.
He is standing in front of the house.
The car is behind the house.
There are flowers in the middle of the table.
There are trees around the house.
People are standing all around.
There are many shops nearby.
I am going with my friend.
She is talking with her mother.
One cannot live without water.

words.en: goes / can be done / is possible

phrases.bn: শুক্রবার বাদে আমি প্রতিদিন কাজ করি।
phrases.pronunciation: shukrobar bade ami protidin kaj kori
phrases.en: I work every day except Friday.
Everyone came except you.
This is for you.
He addressed the nation.
He shows respect toward the teacher.
He is walking toward the door.
The train is heading toward Dhaka.
I worked until night.
He stayed awake until morning.
I returned from school.
This river comes from the mountains.
He is taller than me.
He runs faster than I do.
The results are better compared with last year.
He is brave like a tiger.
Think like me.
He works as a teacher.
He came as a guest.

phrases.bn: তাকে নেতা হিসেবে বেছে নেওয়া হয়েছে।
phrases.pronunciation: take neta hishebe beche neoya hoyechhe
phrases.en: He was chosen as the leader.
The book was written by Rabindranath.
I write with a pen.
We learn through the internet.
I received the news through a friend.
The road passes through the forest.
The airplane flew over the city.

phrases.bn: পানি সেতুর নিচ দিয়ে প্রবাহিত হয়।
phrases.pronunciation: pani setur nich diye probahito hoy
phrases.en: Water flows underneath the bridge.
Everyone spoke against injustice.
He voted against the proposal.
I am in your favor.
The decision is in our favor.
There is a shop opposite the bank.
Everyone stood before him.
There is a village near the river.
There is a field adjacent to the school.
A road runs along the river.
Everyone stood around him.
Joy filled the house throughout.
Celebrations are happening across the country.
The event will continue throughout the year.
Work according to the rules.
Everything happened according to the plan.
A decision will be made with respect to the situation.
I'll speak later regarding this matter.
We are studying about history.
He gave a lecture on science.
They are talking about the movie.
He came along with his family.
He discussed it with his friend.
He spoke with respect.

phrases.bn: কাজ ব্যতীত সে কিছু ভাবছে না।
phrases.pronunciation: kaj bjotit she kichhu bhabochhe na
phrases.en: He is thinking of nothing except work.
He received a bonus in addition to his salary.
Rest after the meal.
Wash your hands before work.
Everyone arrived before the meeting.
We play after school.
The exam will be next week.
The table of contents is at the beginning of the book.
Everyone was happy at the end of the story.
He rested during the work.
They played despite the rain.
He studied even after work.
Drink coffee instead of tea.
Use a card instead of cash.
Entry without permission is prohibited.
He took nothing in exchange for his help.
He is sitting in anticipation of his friend.
The school is close to the station.
Besides work, he also studies.

vocab.sourcePhrase: শুক্রবার বাদে আমি প্রতিদিন কাজ করি।
তাকে নেতা হিসেবে বেছে নেওয়া হয়েছে।
পানি সেতুর নিচ দিয়ে প্রবাহিত হয়।
কাজ ব্যতীত সে কিছু ভাবছে না।

notes: Most Bengali equivalents of English prepositions follow the noun, so they are postpositions.
